note: Malaysia, read on the Immigration Department's own pages (imi.gov.my) on 2026-10-30. A foreign artiste filmed or performing in Malaysia applies, from outside Malaysia, through the Ministry of Communications' one-stop centre for foreign filming and performances (PUSPAL), then holds a Visit Pass (Professional) and a visa with reference; the pass is applied for by a sponsor in Malaysia before entry and lasts up to 12 months (kept as the term; the pages don't say it is renewed). The Employment Pass is issued to expatriates approved by the Expatriate Committee or the relevant regulatory agency (read as tied to the sponsor; apply read as either, since the page names no place); no fee or term is on its page. The Entry Permit (permanent residence) lets a foreign national enter and reside without time limit, with a fully foreign national's category among those listed (read as applied for in Malaysia; its fee and the years it asks are in an e-book on a third-party host, not read). The Residence Pass (Regulation 16A, Immigration Regulations 1963) is for a citizen's or permanent resident's family after 3 or 5 years on a long-term pass, RM 500 for five years, and lets its holder work. Whether a pass's years count toward naturalisation isn't on these pages.

sources.title: Immigration Department of Malaysia, Professional Visitor Pass
sources.said: Applications should be submitted by a sponsor in Malaysia prior to the entry of the applicant into the country. The validity of the pass is subjected to the requirement and conditions of Immigration rules and policies for a period not exceeding 12 months. ... All applications for filming by Foreign Film Production Companies and performances by Foreign Artistes must go through a one-stop application center managed by the responsible Ministry. ... Applicants must be outside of Malaysia when submitting the application. ... Applicants are only allowed to enter Malaysia after obtaining approval for their Professional Visit Pass (PLIK) and Visa with Reference (VDR).

sources.title: Immigration Department of Malaysia, Employment Pass
sources.said: This is a process for the issuance of passes to Expatriates who have been approved by the Expatriate Committee (EC) or the relevant regulatory agencies.

sources.title: Immigration Department of Malaysia, Entry Permit
sources.said: ENTRY PERMIT is a document issued by the Immigration Department of Malaysia as a facility for foreign nationals to enter and reside legally in Malaysia without any time limit . ... Fully Foreign National.

sources.title: Immigration Department of Malaysia, Residence Pass
sources.said: Residence Pass is a pass issued to any foreign national who falls under any category specified under Regulation 16A, Immigration Regulations 1963. ... For Category 3, the applicant has resided in Malaysia for at least three (3) years on a valid long term pass; ... Residence Pass RM 500.00 for five years. ... Residence Pass holders are eligible to work, study, and setting up a business without having to convert to another pass, subject to the conditions of other relevant authorities.
